whatThePageStates: This page is a catalogue of the finding types that GuardDuty RDS Protection can generate for anomalous login behavior on supported Amazon Aurora, Amazon RDS, and Aurora Limitless databases. A short intro says these findings carry a Resource Type of RDSDBInstance or RDSLimitlessDB, then a Topics list enumerates nine finding types, each of which gets its own H2 section. Each section gives the finding name, a one-line description of the behavior detected, a Default severity, a 'Feature:' attribution (identical for all nine: RDS login activity monitoring), an explanatory paragraph, and remediation recommendations. There is no table, no Yes/No matrix, no Region list, and no statement anywhere that anything is NOT supported or NOT detected. The only coverage assertion on the page is enumerative: these nine finding types exist for RDS Protection.

features.statuses: 9 supported (present), 0 not-supported, 0 partial; 9+0+0=9. Every value is a positive existence claim: the finding type is documented, therefore GuardDuty RDS Protection can generate it. There is no negative status anywhere on the page - no 'No' column, no 'isn't available', no exclusion note. Absence of a finding type is simply absence, not a stated non-coverage. The nine names, in page order: CredentialAccess:RDS/AnomalousBehavior.SuccessfulLogin, CredentialAccess:RDS/AnomalousBehavior.FailedLogin, CredentialAccess:RDS/AnomalousBehavior.SuccessfulBruteForce, CredentialAccess:RDS/MaliciousIPCaller.SuccessfulLogin, CredentialAccess:RDS/MaliciousIPCaller.FailedLogin, Discovery:RDS/MaliciousIPCaller, CredentialAccess:RDS/TorIPCaller.SuccessfulLogin, CredentialAccess:RDS/TorIPCaller.FailedLogin, Discovery:RDS/TorIPCaller. Independently verified three ways, all agreeing on 9: 9 Topics bullets, 9 H2 finding sections (the 10th H2 is 'See also', which is boilerplate and not a finding), and 9 'Feature:' bullets.
features.scope: One weak second dimension only: every finding is attributed to the same feature/data source, 'RDS login activity monitoring', and the intro scopes all nine to a Resource Type of RDSDBInstance or RDSLimitlessDB. Because that attribution is constant across all nine rows it does not partition the axis and yields no cross-product. Default severity (1 Variable, 1 Low, 4 Medium, 3 High) is a property of each finding, not a coverage scope - it says how bad, never whether covered. No Region dimension, no plan/tier dimension, no scan-method dimension appears on this page.
features.reasoning: The page's unit of claim is the individual finding type: each has its own H2, its own anchor, its own severity and its own description, and the page's whole purpose is to enumerate them. findingType is a catalogue axis because the list is GuardDuty's own published naming, not a universe that exists independently of the service. The alternative axes are all wrong here: resourceType would give 2 (RDSDBInstance, RDSLimitlessDB) but those are mentioned once in prose as an attribute of the findings, not enumerated as a covered set; dataSource would give 1 constant value; region and service are not present at all.

shouldNotExtract: The Topics bullet list is a duplicate table of contents for the nine H2 sections, not a separate set of nine values - counting both gives 18. The 'See also' H2 and its Skills-for-AI-coding-assistants / Agent Toolkit CLI paragraph is site-wide boilerplate and is not a finding type, so the raw H2 count of 10 must be trimmed to 9. 'Default severity' values (Variable, Low, Medium, High) are severity metadata, not coverage statuses - a parser that reads Variable/Low/Medium/High as a status vocabulary invents a four-state scale that does not exist. The severity Note under the first finding lists Low/Medium/High as three conditional sub-cases of one finding; those are not three findings. The per-finding 'Remediation recommendations' prose, the cross-links to rds-protection.md, guardduty_findings-summary.md and the two guardduty-remediate-compromised-database-rds.md anchors, and the inline HTML <a name=...> anchors are all navigation or advice, not coverage. The H3 sentences (e.g. 'A user successfully logged into an RDS database in your account in an anomalous way.') are descriptions of the H2 above them - pairing them with the H2s double-counts.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no partition, and no availability caveat; any per-Region figure taken from this page is fabricated. SERVICE: effectively one, and only implicitly - the page is about GuardDuty RDS Protection covering Amazon Aurora / Amazon RDS / Aurora Limitless databases, but it never enumerates services as an axis with per-service statuses, so it supports no service count beyond the trivial 1. RESOURCE TYPE: two names appear once in the intro, RDSDBInstance and RDSLimitlessDB, stated as the Resource Type these findings carry. That is an attribute of the findings, not an enumerated coverage matrix with statuses - the page gives no per-resource-type Yes/No, so it should not be reported as a resourceType coverage figure of 2. The only dimension this page genuinely measures is findingType, at 9.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting the Topics list AND the H2 sections and reporting 18 finding types instead of 9. Close behind: including the 'See also' H2 in the section count and reporting 10. Third: reading 'Default severity: Variable / Low / Medium / High' as a Yes/No/Partial-style status axis, which would turn severity metadata into a fake coverage split - and specifically reading 'Variable' as 'Partial'. Fourth: harvesting the three Low/Medium/High bullets in the first finding's Note as extra finding types, giving 11 or 12. Fifth: treating the constant 'Feature: RDS login activity monitoring' bullet as a second axis with nine values when it is one value repeated nine times. Sixth: pulling RDSDBInstance and RDSLimitlessDB out of the intro and publishing a resourceType coverage claim of 2 that the page never makes.
